title: Cosmetics Labeling Guide
quote: The ingredients must be listed in descending order of predominance.
summary: The U.S. labeling guide describes ordering rules and exceptions for low-concentration ingredients, color additives, and drug actives. Ingredient position alone does not reveal a precise concentration.
limitations: U.S. labeling context. This reference does not verify any catalog formula or establish product safety.

title: Dermatologists' top tips for relieving dry skin
summary: AAD discusses gentle skin care, moisturizer use after washing, and creams or ointments for dryness. It distinguishes fragrance-free labeling from unscented labeling.
limitations: General educational guidance. It does not test the products in this catalog or determine individual suitability.

title: Topical niacinamide enhances hydrophobicity and resilience of corneocyte envelopes on different facial locations
publisher: International Journal of Cosmetic Science; PubMed PMID 33038007
summary: A 2020 study examined corneocyte-envelope properties and topical niacinamide in a controlled study. The abstract describes a defined study population and endpoints rather than a comparison of the catalog products.
limitations: Abstract-level reference; full text was not accessible during retrieval. Some authors reported commercial affiliations. No catalog-product efficacy or safety conclusion follows.
